# Show me the evidence: what changed in v1.2.0

From v1.1.0 (2026-11-16, `9b1f8f2dc`) to v1.2.0 (2026-11-16, `c8b54457a`), paragraph by paragraph.

14 paragraphs added, 1 removed, 4 changed in place, 70 unchanged. About 639 words added and 21 removed. Insertions are marked like this, deletions like this; unchanged runs are folded to one line; figures appear as their file names.

[← v1.1.0](v1.1.0.md) · [all versions](../show-me-the-evidence.md)

1 unchanged paragraph

Summary: I want to help people I know get jobs, and the best thing I can give them is a website that shows the evidence. Now that anyone can generate a polished CV, hiring managers trust CVs less: in Robert Half's survey 65% said AI-generated applications make skills harder to verify, and in Greenhouse's 91% of recruiters had spotted deception. So the answer is not a better list; it is proof. Show me the work. Show me your thinking. Tell me what you do outside work, what makes you you, and what you think about my industry. And if you are meeting me, make a page for me. So this is the design of a job-seeker cell: a site of seven pages, home, evidence, thinking, me, a page for you, working with me and a recruiter pack, plus the files machines read; an agent team that interviews the person, finds the evidence, drafts in their words, designs a theme that looks like them, tailors a page per application and checks every fact, while the person approves and sends; eight synthetic personas, from a developer to a security engineer, a senior leader and a graduate, each a template anyone can fork onto GitHub Pages; a ladder from a free recipe to a recruiter's cell; and the brief for the team that builds it. The same cell serves virtual and fractional professionals too, a vCISO, a vCTO, a vDPO, a designer or an editor for hire, who sell their judgement and the agent team behind it. The mock-ups are below. They are also the references our agentic sites have been missing.

## Eight personaspeople looking for a job {#personas}

23 unchanged paragraphs, under Make it yours {#yours}, A page for you {#for-you}, For recruiters {#recruiters}

## Virtual professionals {#virtual}

[figure jbs-virtual.webp] Five virtual professionals: a vCISO, a vCTO, a vDPO, a designer and an editor for hire, each with an agent team. | collage

Many of the people I talk to are not looking for one job. They want to be a virtual CISO, a fractional CTO, an outsourced data protection officer, a designer or an editor for several organisations at once. That market already exists. What is new is what they can sell: not only their judgement, but the agentic team they run behind it. A vCISO with agents that keep the audit evidence and draft the questionnaire answers can serve five scale-ups properly instead of two badly. That is a better offer, and it also proves they can run agentic teams, which their clients will soon want to learn from them.

So I added five more personas, synthetic like the others:

• **Helena Brandt, virtual CISO,** for five scale-ups. Her agents collect audit evidence, draft questionnaire answers from an approved library, keep the policies current and draft a one-page board report; she signs every answer and presents every report.

• **Rafael Costa, virtual CTO,** for non-technical founders. His agents review every pull request, watch dependencies and the cloud bill, and write a Friday digest; they never merge, deploy or spend.

• **Priya Shah, virtual DPO,** appointed for eleven organisations. Her agents keep the records of processing current, triage access requests, draft impact assessments and start the 72-hour clock on a breach; she makes every judgement, and the agents see redacted copies by default.

• **Joana Matos, fractional product designer,** a studio of one person and four agents: synthetic users who test every prototype, a prototyper, a keeper that holds the design system in step with the code, and a researcher.

• **Elliot Grant, fractional editor and librarian,** a newsroom for hire: a researcher, a writer, a fact-checker, a librarian and a translator, and nothing published without his edit and the client's approval. He is for the organisations that want to hire a journalist, and get a desk.

[figure jbs-virtual-model.webp] One professional, several clients, an agent team per client with its own policies; the person decides and signs. | concept

Their sites have the same seven pages, with two changes. The home page shows the team behind the person: each agent, what it does, and the human check on it, with a line on what it can touch ([where assist becomes execute](../../where-assist-becomes-execute.md)). And the recruiter pack becomes an engagement pack: the model, how many clients at once, insurance, where the client's data stays, and the agents' written behaviour policies, shared before anything starts. The page for you works even better here: Helena's sketches the first ninety days of ISO 27001 for a health-tech company, Joana's runs fifty synthetic users through a prospect's public sign-up, Elliot's is a sample weekly briefing built from a prospect's members' public news.

Each client gets its own cell, with its own vault, policies and digest ([the cell is the unit](../../the-cell-is-the-unit.md)). That is also how these professionals scale without cutting corners: the agents add capacity, the person stays accountable.

21 unchanged paragraphs, under The pipeline and the team {#pipeline}, From a recipe to a recruiter's cell {#ladder}, For us first {#us}…

1. **The site template.** Seven pages and the machine files, from one content file per person: profile, proofs, case studies, posts, hobbies, manual, pack. Static, fast, accessible, easy to read on a phone, deployable on GitHub Pages, and fork-ready ([fork it](../../fork-it.md)). 2. **Eight themes, then many more.** The eight personas as forkable templates, each a full site with sample content clearly marked. Then a theme per job family: nurse, teacher, lawyer, chef, data scientist, sales, architect, researcher. 3. **The look-back interview** as the front door: voice or text, one question at a time, each dot marked remembered or evidenced ([connect your dots backwards](../../connect-your-dots-backwards.md)). 4. **The evidence-hunter:** finds and checks the person's public work, and asks before it uses anything about a former employer. 5. **"Make it yours":** a designer agent that interviews the person about their tastes and proposes three directions, never the same three twice. 6. **Pages for you:** a tailor agent that reads an employer's public material and drafts the note, the thing made for them and a 90-day plan; unlisted, expiring, anonymised when public; and a version for a meeting, not only an application. 7. **QA as a gate:** facts against evidence, links, privacy, LinkedIn match, accessibility, phone layout, no hidden text, no invented facts. A failed check blocks publishing. 8. **The recruiter pack and the recruiter's cell:** a one-screen pack on every site, and shortlist pages for recruiters, with consent, expiry and client decisions flowing back. 9. **Synthetic users** who review every template: a hiring manager with ten seconds, a recruiter on a phone, a sceptical CTO, a screen-reader user ([synthetic users for your website](../../synthetic-users-for-your-website.md)). 10. **The ladder on the cell's page:** the recipe and the fork free, then set up, coached, a team, a recruiter's cell, with the side panel from [the cell is the unit](../../the-cell-is-the-unit.md). 11. **A weekly debrief for the search:** applications, replies, what worked, what to tailor next, for the person and nobody else. 12. **A hub of examples:** every template and every real site whose owner agrees, listed on the hub ([a hub for agentic sites](../../a-hub-for-agentic-sites.md)). 13. **Virtual professionals:** the agent-team block and the engagement pack as options in the template; per-client cells with their own vault, policies and digest; themes for vCISO, vCTO, vDPO, designer and editor first, then legal, finance, HR and marketing. 14. **Ourselves first:** sites for me and for team members who want one, each reviewed by its owner before it goes live.
